## Findings

### 1. Corpus inclusion rule
The generator (`load_result_sets`, L222-265) includes every non-dot directory in `results/` containing `summary.json`; `--exclude-results` is invocation-time only. All **53** dirs on disk have `summary.json` → none excluded by rule. The latest viewer (`viewer_2026-06-11i.html`) recorded `results_excluded: []` and embeds 52 sets — `20260611_124829` (4 Fable runs) landed after generation; the "51 sets" figure was an earlier generation. My universe: 53 sets, **2,493 runs** (all `session_id`s unique), 1,530 OpenRouter / 963 Anthropic.

### 2. Timestamps, timezone, tolerance
- **Source: transcript.jsonl for all 2,493 runs** (zero mtime fallbacks). Critical wrinkle: transcripts are seeded with fixture history — unrelated sessions share an identical first-line stamp (`2026-06-08T02:11:49.218Z`) — so first-line timestamps are unusable. Window = `[last stamped line − duration_s, last stamped line]`.
- **304 stalled runs (0 turns + error)** contain *only* fixture content; their windows were stripped (they reflect fixture recording time, e.g. three "runs" ending 06-08 02:13, before the CSV span starts).
- **Timezone:** hourly offset scan (−12..+12h) on Gemini 3.1 Pro: offset 0h attributes **96.7%** of rows; next best (−3h) only 17.2%. CSV `created_at` is **UTC confirmed**.
- **Tolerance: ±120s** — covers billing-meter skew plus generations completing after the final transcript stamp (`generation_time_ms` reaches ~100s). Sensitivity at ±60s moves attribution only 1–3pp and calibration ratios ≤0.05 → robust.

### 3. Attribution coverage and exclusions
Excluded as identifiable non-corpus spend: **static** — gemini-3.5-flash + anthropic/* probes (764 rows, $59.66); **pre-campaign** — unmatched rows before the first corpus run window (06-08 21:44:52 UTC): 4,384 rows, **$66.62** (GLM $33.86 — the confirmed prelim GLM tests, at 18:04–18:17; plus DS Flash $12.61, Qwen $9.94, Flash Lite $6.96, Gemma 26B $3.06 — clusters 16:26–20:10, all predating the first set).

Attributed: **$303.33** across 10 models. Per-model coverage (rows / $): DS Flash 87/86%, DS Pro 96/95%, GLM 93/93%, Flash Lite 90/86%, Gemini Pro 97/96%, Gemma 26B 98/97%, Gemma 31B 95/94%, Kimi 91/89%, **Nemotron 68/68%**, Qwen 95/94%.

Residual orphans: 858 rows, **$27.11** (~8% of attributed) in 7 clusters: 06-10 01:47–02:21 ($8.98) and 04:07–04:10 ($8.74) have **no corpus sets at those times** → deleted throwaway sets/erroneous reruns; 06-09 00:29–01:20 nemotron/GLM ($8.3) overlaps the stalled-run-heavy sets → likely 0-turn stalled runs whose requests still billed server-side (explains Nemotron's lower coverage). Acceptable noise per dispatch.

### 4. Calibration — how wrong is harness cost (billed ÷ harness, attributed/covered runs)
| Model | ratio | realized $/Mtok |
|---|---|---|
| Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite | **0.99** | 0.25 |
| Gemini 3.1 Pro | **1.12** | 2.07 |
| Qwen 3.6 27B | **1.13** | 0.32 |
| Gemma 4 31B | **1.22** | 0.15 |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash | **1.54** | 0.13 |
| Kimi K2.6 | **1.56** | 0.70 |
| Nemotron 3 Ultra | **1.70** | 0.52 |
| GLM 5.1 | **1.78** | 1.05 |
| Gemma 4 26B | **2.30** | 0.13 |
| DeepSeek V4 Pro | **5.55** | 1.62 |

Overall **1.57×** ($303 billed vs $193 harness). DS Pro's 5.55 is regime-mixed: its pricing was corrected ×3.31 on 06-10 (models.yaml comment) but most DS Pro runs predate the fix; at corrected rates the implied ratio is ≈1.68, in line with peers. Two error sources separate cleanly via obs/pred (§6): tokenizer/cache undercounting (most models) vs wrong published rates (Gemma 26B ≈2.1×, DS Flash ≈1.34×, Gemma 31B ≈1.26× understate actual billing).

### 5. Anthropic per-run + Fable
| Model | runs | $/run | tok/run (in+out+cr+cc) | out/run | vis chars/out-tok |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | 141 | 0.034 | 226,901 | 3,051 | 5.00 |
| Sonnet 4.6 | 141 | 0.095 | 208,287 | 2,995 | 5.92 |
| Opus 4.5 | 141 | 0.140 | 189,293 | 2,484 | 5.36 |
| Opus 4.6 | 141 | 0.144 | 191,019 | 2,727 | 5.03 |
| Opus 4.7 | 141 | 0.174 | 234,789 | 3,423 | 4.20 |
| Opus 4.8 | 141 | 0.229 | 301,471 | 4,274 | 3.70 |
| Fable 5 | 117 | 0.518 | 352,358 | 4,562 | 3.18 |

Cost provenance: recomputing with the harness formula (`input·p_in + output·p_out + cache_read·p_cached` — `cost_estimator.py`/`models.py`, which **ignores cache_creation entirely**) reproduces `computed_cost_usd` exactly (ratio 1.000, all 7 models). Under the full Anthropic convention (cache writes at 1.25× input), logged costs are only **0.31–0.36×** true billing — Anthropic-side costs are systematically understated ~3×, dominated by omitted cache-write spend.

**Fable assessment:** output_tokens are NOT anomalously low — Fable has the *highest* output/run and the *lowest* visible-chars-per-output-token (3.18 vs Sonnet 5.92; the thinking-heavy Opus 4.7/4.8 trend the same way at 4.20/3.70). Concealed reasoning therefore appears **included in the usage meter**, so logged costs plausibly DO include concealed-reasoning billing at output rate (modulo the cache-write omission above).

### 6. Token-hunger multiplier prototype

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Gemma 31B | 200,579 | 0.67 | 0.70 | 0.031 | 0.14 | 1.26 | 45.8% |
| Kimi K2.6 | 256,753 | 0.85 | 0.89 | 0.180 | 0.79 | 0.97 | 20.3% |
| Nemotron | 307,192 | 1.02 | 1.06 | 0.160 | 0.70 | 1.00 | 24.2% |

(OpenRouter rows use billed spend/billing-meter tokens over covered runs; Anthropic rows use harness computed cost — itself understated per §5.) **Decomposition:** token hunger spans only 0.67–1.26× Opus 4.8 — cost-per-run divergence is overwhelmingly *price*, not volume. obs/pred ≈ 1.0 for 6 of 10 OpenRouter models means published $/Mtok applied to the *billed* token mix predicts billed cost almost exactly; the harness gap is token *undercounting* (Anthropic tokenizer + ignored cache_creation), except Gemma 26B / DS Flash / Gemma 31B where the published rates themselves are wrong. Timeout truncation: non-timed-out cost/run runs 1.1–1.9× the all-runs figure for high-TO models (JSON `cost_per_run_timeout_split`).

### 7. Caveats (ranked) and recommendation
1. **(High)** DS Pro calibration is pricing-regime-mixed; never apply the blanket 5.55×. 2. **(High)** Published rates for Gemma 26B (~2.1×), DS Flash (~1.34×), Gemma 31B (~1.26×) understate real billing — the viewer's published-pricing display is materially wrong for these. 3. **(Medium)** Attribution is model-level; run-level billed costs aren't separable under same-model concurrency (timeout split uses harness×ratio scaling). 4. **(Medium)** High-TO models' cost/run is truncation-depressed. 5. **(Low)** $27 residual orphans assumed non-corpus. 6. **(Low)** Anthropic-side $ are formula-derived and ~3× understated vs full convention — cross-provider $ comparisons currently mix bases.

**Defensible viewer metrics:** (a) per-model **observed realized $/Mtok** (billed ÷ billing-meter tokens) and (b) **observed billed cost per covered run**, both with ≥85% attribution for 9 of 10 models (Nemotron 68% — flag); and (c) the **token-hunger multiplier vs Opus 4.8**, which is pricing-error-immune. Do not display harness `computed_cost_usd` for either provider without recalibration.
